rv.q: One of the most intelligently sentimental love stories of our time...a nigh perfect production.
Everything about this production is finely judged...Hare's play hits you straight between the eyes with its mixture of private pain and public rage.
Stephen Daldry's production is a debate that dances, a high-velocity encounter between two exceptional actors.

A splendid revival...The actors beautifully trace the arc from the thaw of verbal sparring as Kyra cooks spaghetti bolognese, through rekindled passion to the final bout of full-blooded ideological jousting.
That is emphatically not the case with Skylight, thrillingly revived by Stephen Daldry in a knockout production.
Skylight packs real emotional punch and is often at its funniest when most angry.
It's invigorating stuff, galvanised by the powerful chemistry between them, him the crackling spark, her the poised conductor.
Stephen Daldry ‘s savagely intense production delivers the knottiness and the sentimentality of the idea full blast...

A moving look at politics and love in the emotionally charged revival of David Hare’s Skylight. Many plays become dated after a few years, but not this one. If anything, David Hare’s Skylight has become more pertinent than ever.
Complex, thrilling and provocative, its human heartbeat is just as loud as it ever was.

cn.t: Critics hail Daldry's revival as near-perfect, with Nighy and Mulligan delivering exceptional performances in Hare's emotionally charged debate on love and class inequality that feels strikingly relevant today.
